title: RAW_UNSCREENED: possessive suffix recurrence as an anaphoric participant link
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: test whether recurring suffix-bearing PGP40129 constructions preserve a bound participant relation distinct from article-bearing noun–noun frames, without importing pronoun glosses.

design.architecture: A construction model separates [noun + possessive suffix] from article-bearing noun–noun and modifier frames. The repeated exact source phrase פם מעדתהא is treated as a recurring structural relation; a whole conditional reading carries the bound suffix slot through the record while leaving its antecedent and lexical meaning explicitly unresolved.

source_evidence.quote:
| verso 2 | `פם מעדתהא` | noun plus a possessive suffix on the second noun; exact surface relation recurs below | high for suffix recurrence |
| verso 4 | `פם מעדתהא` | exact repeat of verso 2, within the pomegranate record | high |

design.conditional_whole_reading: After an independently delimited entity or body-part candidate, a suffix-bearing noun carries an anaphoric participant link across a complete clause or record. Exact suffix forms and antecedent alternatives remain recoverable; no English pronoun is assigned.
design.rival: Suffix-bearing words are ordinary lexical/inflectional forms or copied formulae, and all apparent relations are local flat noun sequences with no bound participant slot.
design.falsifier: Suffix-bearing forms fail to recur under any stable source construction, or held antecedent criteria cannot distinguish bound-link and free-local models without occurrence-specific repair.
design.smallest_test: Inventory every suffix-bearing word in the three complete records, freeze repeated and non-repeated cases with offsets, and compare a bound-link model against a free-local rival before any target query.

design.scope_note: Exploratory source-backed architecture only. Exact recurrence on one witness does not establish productive anaphora or a confirmed lexical meaning.
